userStories.title: Declare and thread the no-progress config fields
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add `abortOnNoProgress` and `consecutiveNoProgressToBail` to rectification configuration and carry their resolved values into `RectificationPhaseOptions`.

**Motivation** — The threshold is 3, one higher than the count bail's 2, because this predicate fires on a much wider shape and the true coverage between 179 and 695 iterations cannot be measured until post-#1496 telemetry accrues.

**Approach** — Full threading path: `src/config/schemas-execution.ts` (schema + bounds) → `src/config/schemas.ts` (the default literal) → `src/config/runtime-types.ts` (interface) → `src/cli/config-descriptions.ts` (descriptions) → `src/execution/plan-inputs.ts:426` (build `RectificationPhaseOptions`) → `src/execution/story-orchestrator/types.ts` (option fields) → `rectification.ts:288` (apply).

**Scope** — In: schema declarations, both default declaration sites, runtime and phase-option contracts, CLI descriptions, and plan-input threading. Out: the bail predicate and cycle composition belong to US-002; `src/verification/rectification.ts:32` is a separate legacy consumer and is not modified.

**Interface** — Two new fields on `execution.rectification`:

| Field | Type | Default | Bounds |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `abortOnNoProgress` | boolean | `true` | — |
| `consecutiveNoProgressToBail` | integer | `3` | min 1, max 10 |

**Design note** — **Both declaration sites are required.** `NaxConfigSchema` (`src/config/schemas.ts:113`) passes a hand-maintained object literal to `ExecutionConfigSchema.default(...)`, and Zod does **not** fill in a nested `.default()` for a key that literal omits. Verified against the real schema: `NaxConfigSchema.parse({})` resolves exactly the ten `rectification` keys the literal lists. A field added only to `schemas-execution.ts` therefore resolves to `undefined` — falsy — and the bail would ship permanently dead for every user without an explicit `execution.rectification` block. AC-1.1 and AC-1.2 pin this.
acceptanceCriteria: When `NaxConfigSchema.parse({})` is called, then `execution.rectification.abortOnNoProgress` equals `true`.
When `NaxConfigSchema.parse({})` is called, then `execution.rectification.consecutiveNoProgressToBail` equals `3`.
When `NaxConfigSchema` parses `execution.rectification.consecutiveNoProgressToBail` equal to `0`, then validation fails.
When `NaxConfigSchema` parses `execution.rectification.consecutiveNoProgressToBail` equal to `11`, then validation fails.
When `NaxConfigSchema` parses `execution.rectification.consecutiveNoProgressToBail` equal to `1`, then parsing succeeds.
When `NaxConfigSchema` parses `execution.rectification.consecutiveNoProgressToBail` equal to `10`, then parsing succeeds.

Given a config whose rectification block has `enabled: true`, `abortOnNoProgress: false`, and `consecutiveNoProgressToBail: 7`, when rectification phase options are built, then the resulting `RectificationPhaseOptions.abortOnNoProgress` equals `false`.

Given a config whose rectification block has `enabled: true`, `abortOnNoProgress: false`, and `consecutiveNoProgressToBail: 7`, when rectification phase options are built, then the resulting `RectificationPhaseOptions.consecutiveNoProgressToBail` equals `7`.
When `NaxConfigSchema` parses an explicit `execution.rectification.abortOnNoProgress: false`, then the resolved value equals `false`.

routing.reasoning: This is standard additive multi-file configuration threading with clear defaults, validation bounds, and a single consumer contract.

outOfScope: The bail predicate and cycle composition belong to US-002.

`src/verification/rectification.ts:32` is a separate legacy consumer of `abortOnIncreasingFailures` in the verification lane, comparing `currentFailures` against `initialFailures`. It is a different lane and is not modified by this spec.

modifiedFiles.reason: declare both fields with their bounds
add both keys to the `ExecutionConfigSchema.default(...)` literal
add both fields to the rectification interface

userStories.title: Add and wire the identity-keyed no-progress bail
acceptanceCriteria: Given `withNoProgressBail` imported from `@/execution`, enabled with threshold `3`, and three trailing iterations with the identical single finding in `findingsBefore` and `findingsAfter`, when the wrapped strategy's `bailWhen` is called, then it returns a non-null reason string.
Given five iterations that each start with five findings and end with a different one removed, when the wrapped strategy's `bailWhen` is called, then it returns `null`.
Given a no-progress threshold of `3` and exactly two no-progress iterations, when the wrapped strategy's `bailWhen` is called, then it returns `null`.

Given a no-progress threshold of `3` and a third no-progress iteration appended to two trailing no-progress iterations, when the wrapped strategy's `bailWhen` is called, then it returns a non-null reason string.

Given three trailing iterations whose before keys all persist after and whose after sets also contain two additional findings, when the wrapped strategy's `bailWhen` is called, then it returns a non-null reason string.
When `withNoProgressBail` is called with `enabled` set to `false`, then it returns strategy entries that are the same objects passed in.
When `withNoProgressBail` is called with `enabled` set to `false`, then each returned strategy's `bailWhen` is unchanged.
Given an input strategy whose `bailWhen` returns `"user-stop"` and three no-progress iterations, when the wrapped strategy's `bailWhen` is called, then it returns `"user-stop"`.
Given three trailing iterations whose `findingsBefore` arrays are empty, when the wrapped strategy's `bailWhen` is called, then it returns `null`.
Given three no-progress iterations carrying two persisting findings, when the wrapped strategy's `bailWhen` is called, then its non-null reason reports iteration count `3`.
Given three no-progress iterations carrying two persisting findings, when the wrapped strategy's `bailWhen` is called, then its non-null reason reports persisting-finding count `2`.

Given `runRectification` uses `enabled: true`, at least one rectification validation phase collected, `abortOnNoProgress: true`, `consecutiveNoProgressToBail: 3`, `maxAttemptsTotal: 12`, and validation always returns the same two findings, when the cycle runs, then `RectificationResult.rectificationExhausted` equals `true`.

Given `runRectification` uses `enabled: true`, at least one rectification validation phase collected, `abortOnNoProgress: true`, `consecutiveNoProgressToBail: 3`, `maxAttemptsTotal: 12`, and validation always returns the same two findings, when the cycle runs, then its rectification strategy fix operation is dispatched exactly `3` times.

Given `runRectification` uses `enabled: true`, at least one rectification validation phase collected, `abortOnNoProgress: false`, `maxAttemptsTotal: 12`, and validation always returns the same two findings, when the cycle runs, then its rectification strategy fix operation is dispatched more than `3` times.

Given three trailing iterations simultaneously satisfy no-progress and count-increase and both wrappers are enabled at threshold `3`, when `withNoProgressBail` wraps `withIncreasingFailuresBail` and `bailWhen` is called, then it returns the no-progress reason rather than the count-increase reason.

routing.reasoning: This adds one small pure wrapper plus established barrel and rectification wiring; targeted unit cases and the existing rectification-overrides harness cover the priority-sensitive integration without requiring a heavier workflow.

outOfScope: US-001 owns declaration and threading of `abortOnNoProgress` and `consecutiveNoProgressToBail`.
`withIncreasingFailuresBail` and its predicate, reason string, and existing tests are not modified; the count bail's behaviour is preserved exactly.
`classifyOutcome` (`src/findings/cycle.ts:72`) is correct and is not modified. The new predicate reads finding arrays directly rather than branching on the `outcome` label.

`src/verification/rectification.ts:32` is a separate legacy consumer of `abortOnIncreasingFailures` in the verification lane, comparing `currentFailures` against `initialFailures`. It is a different lane and is not modified by this spec.

modifiedFiles.reason: compose the new wrapper around the existing one

analysis: This is an additive, backward-compatible enhancement to the existing story-orchestrator rectification loop, not a greenfield feature. The current count-based wrapper is `withIncreasingFailuresBail` in `src/execution/story-orchestrator/run-phase.ts:429-452`; it returns the input strategy array unchanged when disabled, delegates to a strategy's existing `bailWhen` first, clamps its threshold to one, and otherwise bails only when every trailing iteration has a larger `findingsAfter` count. `runRectification` constructs the production `FixCycle` in `src/execution/story-orchestrator/rectification.ts:287-302` and currently applies that one wrapper before calling `runFixCycle`. The new composition must make the observable priority user-supplied predicate, no-progress, then count-increase; merely calling the already-wrapped count predicate first would incorrectly mask the required no-progress diagnosis. `runRectification` returns exhaustion for an exhausted cycle with final findings at `src/execution/story-orchestrator/rectification.ts:450-457`, and it records iteration count/exit reason in phase output at lines 418-423, so the production seam should assert fix-operation dispatch count rather than require a new result field. Finding identity is already canonicalized by `findingKey` at `src/findings/types.ts:245-247`, serializing source, file, line, rule, and message; message drift intentionally appears as progress, making the new bail conservative. `RectificationPhaseOptions` in `src/execution/story-orchestrator/types.ts:22-32` already carries the increasing-failure fields; `assemblePlanInputsFromCtx` builds the option object at `src/execution/plan-inputs.ts:422-429`. Config has a multi-site contract: `RectificationConfigSchema` declares the neighboring increasing-failure fields at `src/config/schemas-execution.ts:60-66`, while `NaxConfigSchema` supplies a separate complete default object at `src/config/schemas.ts:120-131`. The latter must include both new values or parsing `{}` leaves them absent despite schema field defaults. The runtime interface and CLI descriptions are neighboring declarations at `src/config/runtime-types.ts:61-65` and `src/cli/config-descriptions.ts:81-83`. Relevant existing tests include `test/unit/config/schemas.test.ts` for parsing, `test/unit/execution/plan-inputs.test.ts` for plan assembly, and `test/unit/execution/rectification-overrides.test.ts` for the `runRectification` harness. `src/execution/index.ts` re-exports story-orchestrator symbols through `src/execution/story-orchestrator/index.ts`, so the new public symbol must follow that two-barrel path. Add focused unit coverage for the new wrapper and config threading, plus integration-level production-path coverage through the existing overrides harness. Risks are wrapper-precedence regression, accidental mutation/allocation when the feature flag is off, a vacuous empty-before-set bail, and changing the legacy count predicate or verification-lane retry behavior. Migration is configuration-only: defaults enable the conservative three-iteration bail for existing users; users can opt out with `execution.rectification.abortOnNoProgress: false`, and no persisted data or config migration is required.
outOfScope: The R1 story-scoped attempt budget and decline ledger (the fix cycle's budget remains per-cycle) is deferred to a separate arc.

The R4 oscillation circuit-breaker rework — counting oscillation at finding identity rather than at `source`, and reading the breaker mid-story rather than only on the story-failure path — is deferred; its 158/57 split must be re-probed after R1 lands before it can be sized.
The R2 experiment of restating prior fix attempts explicitly in the fix prompt is deferred; its benefit is unproven and it is to be run as a measured experiment, not shipped as a fix.

`src/verification/rectification.ts:32` is a separate legacy consumer of `abortOnIncreasingFailures` in the verification lane, comparing `currentFailures` against `initialFailures`. It is a different lane and is not modified by this spec.
`withIncreasingFailuresBail` and its predicate, reason string, and existing tests are not modified; the count bail's behaviour is preserved exactly.
`classifyOutcome` (`src/findings/cycle.ts:72`) is correct and is not modified. The new predicate reads finding arrays directly rather than branching on the `outcome` label.
No change to reviewer prompts, finding classification, retirement, or cost/budget accounting.
Retroactive measurement of how many historical iterations the new predicate would have caught is not possible from pre-#1496 records (which carry counts only) and is not attempted.
